statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5324 — Structuring transactions to evade reporting requirements?
statutory.answer: No. 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements, but these facts do not show transactions structured around the $10,000 CTR threshold or an intent to evade reporting.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits (among other things) causing or attempting to cause a domestic financial institution to fail to file a required report, causing or attempting to cause a report to contain a material omission/misstatement, or structuring/assisting in structuring (or attempting) any transaction with one or more domestic financial institutions for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements (i.e., the CTR regime triggered by cash transactions over $10,000). Here, the listed activity includes many cash transactions far above $10,000 (e.g., $21,672.90; $30,540.63; $42,279.82; $46,095.25), which would ordinarily trigger CTR filing rather than evade it; there is no pattern of breaking cash into multiple sub-$10,000 transactions on the same day or in close succession to avoid the threshold, and no facts indicating the actor’s purpose was to evade reporting or that any bank was caused to not file or to file falsely. Because § 5324’s key elements—structuring around the reporting threshold and purpose to evade (or causing non-filing/false filing)—are not supported by the fact pattern, the conduct described does not fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5324.
